meta.title: Free Reading for Less
meta.description: A hand-checked directory of genuinely free reading and listening: library ebook and audio apps, public-domain libraries, open textbooks, language-learning freebies, and big-library cards almost anyone can get.
meta.generatedNotice: Data is embedded into index.html by tools/build.js. Edit data/sites.json, then rebuild.
meta.freePolicy: This directory contains no affiliate links, no referral codes, and no paid placements. Every card earns its place.

sites.name: Libby (OverDrive)
sites.whatItIs: The main app most U.S. public libraries use to lend ebooks, audiobooks, and digital magazines.
sites.whatsFree: Every borrow, hold, and read/listen. No subscription at any point.
sites.signup: A library card from a participating library (usually free for your own county or city residents).
sites.honestLimits: Popular new titles have waits and holds. Loan periods (typically 7–21 days) are set by your library. You need a real card — most systems prove residency, and some charge non-residents.
sites.notes: Also handles Kindle delivery in the U.S. for ebook titles where the publisher allows it.

sites.name: Hoopla
sites.whatItIs: A companion service to Libby used by thousands of libraries, offering instant-borrow ebooks, audiobooks, comics, movies, and music.
sites.whatsFree: All borrowing is free through your participating library.
sites.signup: A library card from a library that subscribes to Hoopla (signup takes about a minute).
sites.honestLimits: Borrows per month are capped (often 3–10, library's choice). No holds — titles are always available — but the catalog is mostly midlist and backlist, not current bestsellers.
sites.notes: Great for always-available audiobooks when every Libby copy is on hold.

sites.name: Project Gutenberg
sites.whatItIs: The oldest digital library: over 75,000 public-domain books built to endure 'as long as language itself'.
sites.whatsFree: Everything — download to your heart's content, in the U.S. and most other countries.
sites.signup: None. No account, no email, no ads — browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Public domain means classics, not recent releases. Copyright terms differ by country, so a book free in the U.S. may not be free where you live.
sites.notes: No registration, no fees, no ads. The strictest definition of genuinely free.

sites.name: Standard Ebooks
sites.whatItIs: Volunteer editors take Gutenberg texts and produce gorgeously typeset, carefully proofread epub and Kindle editions.
sites.whatsFree: All ebooks, under a CC0/public-domain dedication. The whole repo is on GitHub too.
sites.signup: None required for reading. The editing source lives on GitHub if you want to help.
sites.honestLimits: Only public-domain authors (Austen, Dickens, Lovecraft, etc.). New titles appear weekly, but don't expect modern books.
sites.notes: Probably the best-looking free classics you'll ever put on an e-reader.

sites.name: Internet Archive
sites.whatItIs: A giant non-profit library of scanned books, recordings, films, and websites.
sites.whatsFree: Millions of fully public-domain scans you can download outright, plus free account access.
sites.signup: Free account (email) only for lending modern books; public-domain downloads need nothing.
sites.honestLimits: Modern in-copyright books are lent with one-reader-per-copy waitlists, and publishers have sued over this model — that part of the catalog can change in court. Public-domain material is safe.
sites.notes: Also hosts LibriVox audio and old radio/newsreel material. A nonprofit — no affiliate links.

sites.name: Open Library
sites.whatItIs: An Internet Archive project: one web page for every book ever published, with borrowable digital copies for many.
sites.whatsFree: Catalog is free; classic pre-1928 books can be read online freely; modern titles borrow with a free account.
sites.signup: Free account (email) to borrow; reading public-domain classics is open.
sites.honestLimits: Each lendable digital copy serves one reader at a time, so expect hold lists for popular modern books (typically ~2 weeks per loan).
sites.notes: Excellent as a 'does a free scan exist?' checker before you buy anything.

sites.name: Wikisource
sites.whatItIs: Wikimedia's library of source texts: historical documents, speeches, laws, and public-domain works in many languages.
sites.whatsFree: Everything, forever, no account needed to read.
sites.signup: None for reading. A Wikimedia account only to edit.
sites.honestLimits: Coverage is uneven — famous documents are excellent, obscure books less so. Text-only, no typeset downloads.
sites.notes: Also serves as the home of the multilingual portal linking language-specific Wikisources.

sites.name: LibriVox
sites.whatItIs: Volunteer-read public-domain audiobooks: over 20,000 titles recorded by volunteers and given away free.
sites.whatsFree: All downloads, all formats (mp3, m4b, RSS feed). No ads, no account.
sites.signup: None. No account, no signup.
sites.honestLimits: Narration quality varies by volunteer — some are wonderful, some are rough. Only public-domain books.
sites.notes: Search by reader if you find a volunteer whose voice you like.

sites.name: Lit2Go
sites.whatItIs: A University of South Florida project pairing public-domain stories and poems with free mp3s and printable texts.
sites.whatsFree: Everything, including downloadable passages and reading-comprehension materials.
sites.signup: None. Browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Public-domain works only; the catalog skews toward classics often used in schools.
sites.notes: Specifies reading level (Flesch-Kincaid) for many passages — handy for parents and ESL readers.

sites.name: Loyal Books
sites.whatItIs: A free audiobook catalog of public-domain recordings (largely LibriVox and similar projects) organized in a friendlier interface.
sites.whatsFree: All downloads, mp3 and rss.
sites.signup: None. Browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Same limits as any volunteer-read public-domain catalog: no modern bestsellers, quality varies.
sites.notes: Includes non-English audio in a handful of languages.

sites.name: OpenStax
sites.whatItIs: Rice University's peer-reviewed, openly licensed college textbooks (biology, chemistry, physics, economics, psychology, math...).
sites.whatsFree: Free web view, PDF, and cheap print. Instructor materials for verified instructors.
sites.signup: None for students. Instructors verify an institutional email for answer keys.
sites.honestLimits: Intro-level college subjects only. Problem sets sometimes reference paid online homework systems that are NOT free — ignore those and the book is fully free.
sites.notes: Funded by philanthropy, not ads; no affiliate anything.

sites.name: Open Textbook Library
sites.whatItIs: University of Minnesota's searchable catalog of openly licensed textbooks across dozens of disciplines, with faculty reviews.
sites.whatsFree: All listed books are free to download and keep.
sites.signup: None. Browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Quality varies between titles; read the published reviews. Some books are niche.
sites.notes: A great first stop before paying $150 for a survey textbook.

sites.name: MIT OpenCourseWare
sites.whatItIs: MIT's free publication of 2,500+ real courses — lecture notes, assignments, some video.
sites.whatsFree: All course materials, no account, no fees.
sites.signup: None. Browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: No credit, no instructor, no certificate unless you bypass to paid options. Some courses are text-heavy rather than video.
sites.notes: Pairs perfectly with a free OpenStax textbook for the reading stack.

sites.name: Saylor Academy
sites.whatItIs: A nonprofit offering free self-paced courses built on openly licensed materials, with optional free certificates.
sites.whatsFree: Every course, plus free (non-credit) certificates on passing.
sites.signup: None to browse. Free account only for graded quizzes and certificates.
sites.honestLimits: Self-graded pace, no instructor feedback. Certificates aren't college credit, though a few courses can be recommended for credit by third parties.
sites.notes: Solid for business, accounting, and computer-science refreshers.

sites.name: Duolingo (free tier)
sites.whatItIs: The famous bite-sized language app — and its core course content genuinely is free.
sites.whatsFree: The full course tree for 40+ languages on web and mobile, with ads.
sites.signup: Free account via email or Google. Upgrade is optional and never required.
sites.honestLimits: Ads and 'hearts' penalties push you toward Super Duolingo ($). It's persuasion-by-annoyance, not a paywall: patience or a web session works. Fewer languages with less depth than a school course.
sites.notes: Do daily, but pair it with real reading (see the free library apps above).

sites.name: Language Transfer
sites.whatItIs: Completely free 'thinking method' audio courses (Spanish, French, Arabic, Turkish, Greek, Italian, German, Swahili...) made by one volunteer-funded nonprofit.
sites.whatsFree: Everything — every lesson audio, offline downloads, no ads, no account.
sites.signup: None. Stream or download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Limited language list and it's audio-only; you must actually think along, not passively listen.
sites.notes: Funded purely by donations. If it clicks for you, consider donating (that's their site, not an affiliate link).

sites.name: Live Lingua Project
sites.whatItIs: Free hosting of the U.S. Foreign Service Institute and Defense Language Institute public-domain courses: full textbooks plus recorded drills.
sites.whatsFree: All course PDFs and mp3s.
sites.signup: None. Browse and download directly.
sites.honestLimits: Materials can be decades old (some dated vocabulary and gendered examples), and they're kitted out like 1960s language labs — because they are.
sites.notes: The most rigorous free language training that exists; treat it as a serious course, not an app.

sites.name: Brooklyn Public Library eCard
sites.whatItIs: Brooklyn's digital-only library card, which unlocks Libby collections of one of the biggest library systems in the U.S.
sites.whatsFree: The eCard itself is free, instantly by email, for New York State residents age 13+.
sites.signup: Online form with a New York State address and birthdate.
sites.honestLimits: Only for people who live in New York State. eCards can access digital collections only, not physical branches; policies can change, so verify at the source before relying on it.
sites.notes: A common trick: pair it with your local card to double your Libby catalog.

sites.name: Your own county library card
sites.whatItIs: The single highest-value free reading resource you already own access to: your home public library's ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, movies, and newspapers.
sites.whatsFree: Card and all digital services for residents — often online signup with instant approval.
sites.signup: One photo ID plus proof of residency at your local branch, or an online form for instant digital access.
sites.honestLimits: Residency rules apply; non-resident fees exist in some places (though many systems offer reasonably priced non-resident cards worth it for one year).
sites.notes: Everylibrary links to advocacy; use your own system's site for signup details. This entry links to a nonprofit, not a paid listing.

sites.name: NLS BARD (Braille and Audio Reading Download)
sites.whatItIs: The Library of Congress's program lending braille and audio books free to U.S. residents with qualifying visual, physical, or reading disabilities.
sites.whatsFree: Everything for eligible readers: device loans, braille, tens of thousands of downloadable audio titles.
sites.signup: Application certified by a doctor, librarian, or qualified professional; handled through your state network library.
sites.honestLimits: Eligibility requirements apply — it's designed for people who can't read standard print comfortably, not open enrollment.
sites.notes: Healthcare workers: BARD is often unknown to patients who qualify for it. A plain-language tip worth passing along.

sites.name: Library of Congress Digital Collections
sites.whatItIs: Primary-source treasure chest: digitized letters, photographs, maps, sound recordings, and historic books from the national library.
sites.whatsFree: All publicly available items; no account needed.
sites.signup: None to browse. Researchers may request archival access separately.
sites.honestLimits: It's a research collection, not a reader's shelf — you browse themes like a museum. Some materials have specific rights notices.
sites.notes: Fantastic for authors (like ours) who write nonfiction and want free primary sources.

sites.name: Open Culture
sites.whatItIs: A long-running nonprofit-minded blog curating 'the best free cultural & educational media' — free ebooks, audiobooks, courses, and films.
sites.whatsFree: The curation is free; everything it links out to is a free resource.
sites.signup: None. Newsletter signup is optional and you can skip it.
sites.honestLimits: It's a link blog: quality is curated but you end up at other sites whose terms can change. Occasional donation asks, no affiliate selling of the free lists.
sites.notes: Their '800 Free eBooks' and '1,000 Free Audio Books' posts are perennial deep-dive indexes.
